name: Quest ordering
description: Composes the hub's stated_fields arm (called through hubofhubs.api) and overrides only Quest's own rules. Everything generic is the hub's: what the person stated, a blocked item after the unblocked, the deadline, the age of an ask, people waiting, what answering an ask or reaching a milestone frees, effort, met milestones and the batch limit. What Quest adds, handed to the hub in the fields it reads: a person's rank map with the creator's legacy rank counting only for the creator, open asks before goals before ideas for the work to start, the shorter goal horizon before the deadline, completed goals after open ones, a goal the AI rep handles after the person's own, undated asks put to the person newest first, a metric measured longest ago first. It orders the three subjects of the hub (work, asks, goals) and three goal levels: solution milestones, a quest's period goals and the day's goals, which are tasks. Scheduling a day has no rule or case in Quest yet and is not ordered here. One to one: a period goal is the milestone of the solution it is for, linked by Quest's spec_solution_id (a goal's spec_metric_id and metric_target_value are optional), and is ordered as that milestone, with no ranking of its own.
advantages: Passes every foundation case of the hub and reproduces every rule Quest writes down in its own code and tests, free and repeatable; a change to the hub's generic rules reaches Quest without a copy.
disadvantages: Quest's horizon, completed and rep-handled marks are folded with the person's rank into the one rank the hub reads, so a blocked goal still comes after an unblocked one, completed or not, as in the hub.
